title: Odia Dhaga · ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଢଗଢମାଳି
subtitle: Sayings, meanings and the sources behind them
scope_note: A growing research repository: 108 explained sayings with traceable contemporary witnesses, historical comparisons and a source survey for expansion. This is not a complete anthology or a certified public-domain corpus. Public access, open licensing and historical attestation are recorded separately.
license: Original Project Odisha commentary and illustrations: CC BY-SA4.0. Wikimedia-derived entries retain their attributed CC BY-SA4.0 terms. Three short SCERT quotations have separate source rights and are not openly licensed or relicensed here. Fonts and other source material retain their own rights.
editorial_note: By Ahimanikya Satapathy · Project Odisha. AI-assisted research and drafting; separate AI review is recorded in the research handoff and is not human or community validation. See README.md for method and limits.

sources.title: ଢଗମାଳିକା, ପ୍ରଥମଭାଗ
sources.locator: 19 PDF pages; numbered proverb text begins PDF2, apparent printed1.
sources.access: Title and first three text pages viewed as rendered images. OCR downloaded but seriously inaccurate.
sources.rights: Publicly accessible scan from Srujanika/Odia Bibhaba, uploaded2024. No rights field in inspected IA metadata. Underlying1893 text is a strong public-domain candidate, but publisher-only credit means author identification still unresolved; this report does not certify worldwide public-domain status. Digital watermark is provenance, not reuse licence.
sources.limits: Title and selected sayings visually checked. Three entries have located historical versions; the volume has not been completely transcribed. Historical readings retain explicit glyph/spacing uncertainty and unresolved reuse status.
sources.bibliography: Title page explicitly says published by Sri Gobinda Rath, Cuttack, Victoria Press, 1893. Metadata says Gobinda Rath, publisher. Do not silently convert publisher to author.
